title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 97
paragraphs: While they held these thoughts and had been set at enmity with the Persians, at this very time Aristagoras the Milesian, ordered away from Sparta by Cleomenes the Lacedaemonian, arrived in Athens; for this was the most powerful city besides Sparta. Aristagoras came forward before the popular assembly and said the same things he had said at Sparta about the wealth in Asia and about the Persian manner of fighting—how they used neither shield nor spear and were easy to overcome. Thus he spoke, and he added that the Milesians were colonists from the Athenians and that it was only reasonable for the Athenians to rescue them, since they had such great power; and there was nothing he did not promise, being very pressing in his request, until at last he persuaded them. For it seems that it is easier to deceive many than one, since, though he was not able by himself to deceive Cleomenes the Lacedaemonian, he did just that to thirty thousand Athenians. Being persuaded, the Athenians voted a resolution to send twenty ships to help the Ionians, and appointed to command them Melanthius, one of their citizens, who was highly regarded in all things. These ships proved to be the beginning of evils for the Hellenes and the barbarians.
